questions.question: When the Fa'il (subject) comes after the verb (Mu'akhkhar), which aspect of verb agreement is dropped entirely?
options: Neither — the verb fully agrees with the Fa'il in both number and gender
Both number and gender agreement — the verb takes a fixed neutral form
Number agreement — the verb is always singular (Wahid) regardless of the Fa'il
Gender agreement — the verb defaults to Mudhakkar regardless of the Fa'il
questions.explanation: When the Fa'il is Mu'akhkhar, the verb drops number agreement entirely and is always singular (Wahid). However, gender agreement is retained: the verb must match the Fa'il in being Mudhakkar or Mu'annas.

questions.question: What is the rule for verb agreement with جَمْعُ التَّكْسِير غَيْر عَاقِل (Jama' Taksir Ghair 'Aqil)?
options: اخْتِيَارِي (Ikhtiyari) — optional; the speaker may choose singular feminine or plural masculine
لَازِم (Lazim) — obligatory to treat it as singular feminine, no choice
اخْتِيَارِي (Ikhtiyari) — optional but the default is plural masculine if no preference is stated
لَازِم (Lazim) — obligatory to treat it as plural masculine
questions.explanation: For Jama' Taksir Ghair 'Aqil (non-rational broken plural, e.g., الكُتُب), it is Lazim (obligatory) to treat it as singular feminine — the speaker has no choice. This contrasts with Jama' Taksir 'Aqil, where it is Ikhtiyari (optional).

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the two stated reasons for dropping the فَاعِل (Fa'il) from a sentence, thereby creating a Naib al-Fa'il?
options: The sentence already contains a Mubtada that performs the same function
The Fa'il is a pronoun and therefore does not need to be stated explicitly
The verb is intransitive and takes no visible subject
The doer is deliberately concealed — for example, to avoid announcing one's own good deed
questions.explanation: The two reasons for dropping the Fa'il are: (1) the doer is unknown, or (2) the doer is deliberately concealed — for example, saying بُنِيَ الْمَسْجِدُ to avoid announcing that you yourself built the mosque.

questions.question: When a فَصْل (Fasl) appears between a verb and its Mu'annas Fa'il, what does it permit regarding the verb's gender?
options: The verb must be Mu'annas to agree with the Fa'il regardless of the Fasl
The verb may be Mudhakkar (masculine) even though the Fa'il is Mu'annas
The Fa'il may shift to Nasb case instead of Raf'
The verb may take the plural form instead of the singular
questions.explanation: A Fasl removes the direct adjacency between the verb and its Fa'il. When present, the verb is permitted to be Mudhakkar even if the Fa'il is Mu'annas, because the intervening word breaks the proximity required for gender agreement.

questions.question: Mubtada and Khabar take Raf' due to a عَامِل مَعْنَوِي ('Amil Ma'nawi). What is the specific name of this 'Amil?
options: الفِعْل (Al-Fi'l) — the verb present earlier in the discourse
الإِضَافَة (Al-Idafa) — the genitive construction linking the two terms
الاِبْتِدَاء (Al-Ibtida') — the act of beginning a nominal sentence
الحَرْف (Al-Harf) — an implicit particle causing the case change
questions.explanation: The 'Amil for Mubtada and Khabar is Al-Ibtida' — the conceptual act of beginning a nominal sentence. It is called Ma'nawi because it is implicit and not a visible word, unlike the verb that makes the Fa'il Marfu'.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the six conditions under which a نَكِرَة (Nakira) noun may serve as Mubtada?
options: The Nakira has a Sifa (adjective), making it a نَكِرَة مُخَصَّصَة (Nakira Mukhassasa)
The Nakira is in the Nasb case due to a preceding 'Amil
The Nakira is a proper noun used in a general sense
The Nakira immediately follows a Ma'rifa noun in the same sentence
questions.explanation: One of the six conditions is that the Nakira has a Sifa (adjective) qualifying it, making it Nakira Mukhassasa. The specification moves it closer to Ma'rifa, which is the default requirement for Mubtada.

questions.question: نَائِبُ الْفَاعِل (Naib al-Fa'il) always takes which grammatical case (i'rab)?
options: Nasb (accusative)
Raf' (nominative)
Jarr (genitive)
It varies depending on the type of verb
questions.explanation: Naib al-Fa'il is the Maf'ul raised to take the place of the dropped Fa'il in a passive sentence. It always takes Raf' (nominative case), just as the original Fa'il did.

questions.question: When a verb becomes فِعْل مَجْهُول (Fi'l Majhul), what happens to the original فَاعِل (Fa'il)?
options: It is dropped entirely from the sentence
It becomes the Naib al-Fa'il and takes Raf'
It shifts to Nasb case as a secondary object
It remains in the sentence but takes Jarr case
questions.explanation: The passive construction (Fi'l Majhul) is signaled by a vowel change in the verb (e.g., ضَرَبَ → ضُرِبَ). The original Fa'il is dropped entirely, and the Maf'ul is promoted to Naib al-Fa'il in its place.

questions.question: For the purpose of verb agreement, جَمْعُ التَّكْسِير (Jama' Taksir) is classified under which broader grammatical category?
options: مُذَكَّر حَقِيقِي (Mudhakkar Haqiqi) — real masculine
جَمْع مُذَكَّر سَالِم (Jama' Mudhakkar Salim) — sound masculine plural
مُثَنَّى (Muthanna) — dual
مُؤَنَّث غَيْر حَقِيقِي (Mu'annas Ghair Haqiqi) — non-real feminine
questions.explanation: For verb agreement purposes, Jama' Taksir falls under Mu'annas Ghair Haqiqi (non-real feminine). This is why it is treated as singular feminine in agreement — it has the feminine quality without being a genuinely female entity.

questions.question: A فَصْل (Fasl) appears between a verb and a Mu'annas Fa'il. What specifically does this permit regarding the verb?
options: The verb must take the plural form to reflect the distance from its Fa'il
The Fa'il may be omitted entirely when a Fasl is present
The verb may shift from perfect (madi) to imperfect (mudari') form
The verb may be Mudhakkar (masculine) despite the Fa'il being Mu'annas
questions.explanation: A Fasl (intervening word) removes the direct adjacency between the verb and its Fa'il. This permits the verb to be Mudhakkar even when the Fa'il is Mu'annas, as exemplified by أَسْلَمَ الْيَوْمَ سَارَةُ where الْيَوْمَ is the Fasl.

questions.question: What makes a نَكِرَة (Nakira) into a نَكِرَة مُخَصَّصَة (Nakira Mukhassasa), enabling it to function as Mubtada?
options: The presence of a Zarf (adverb) elsewhere in the sentence
The addition of the definite article making it Ma'rifa
A Sifa (adjective) or qualifying element that specifies it
Its position at the very beginning of a nominal sentence
questions.explanation: A Nakira Mukhassasa is a Nakira specified by a Sifa or qualifying element. This specification moves the noun closer to Ma'rifa in definiteness, making it eligible to serve as Mubtada despite the default rule requiring Ma'rifa.

questions.question: Why is the عَامِل (Amil) causing Mubtada and Khabar to take Raf' described as مَعْنَوِي (Ma'nawi) rather than لَفْظِي (Lafzi)?
options: It is conceptual and implicit — not a visible word in the sentence
It applies only to sentences with a specific semantic meaning
It is a later grammatical convention not found in early Arabic poetry
It is a particle (harf) that is often elided in speech but present in writing
questions.explanation: The 'Amil for Mubtada and Khabar is Al-Ibtida' — a conceptual act, not a physical word. A Lafzi 'Amil (like the verb for Fa'il) is visible and explicit, while a Ma'nawi 'Amil is implied and abstract.

questions.question: In the context of Jama' Taksir verb agreement, what does لَازِم (Lazim) indicate about the speaker's choice?
options: The rule is obligatory — the speaker has no choice
The rule is recommended but the speaker may deviate for clarity
The rule is optional and either form is correct
The rule applies only in formal written Arabic, not in speech
questions.explanation: Lazim means obligatory — the speaker has no choice. Jama' Taksir Ghair 'Aqil must be treated as singular feminine in verb agreement; unlike Jama' Taksir 'Aqil, where it is Ikhtiyari (optional).

questions.question: When the Khabar is a Zarf and the Mubtada is a نَكِرَة (Nakira), what must be true about the Khabar's position in the sentence?
options: The Khabar must immediately follow the Mubtada
The Khabar must come last to avoid ambiguity with the Fa'il
The Khabar may appear anywhere in the sentence without restriction
The Khabar must come first (مُقَدَّم) and the Mubtada comes last (مُؤَخَّر)
questions.explanation: When the Khabar is a Zarf and the Mubtada is Nakira, the required word order is Khabar first (Muqaddam) and Mubtada last (Mu'akhkhar). This specific configuration is one of the six conditions permitting a Nakira to serve as Mubtada.

questions.question: What specific contradiction makes the behaviour of the Ahbar in Ayah 44 irrational (أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ)?
options: They performed outward worship while secretly maintaining idol worship
They commanded others to believe in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ while rejecting him themselves
They recited the Torah publicly but claimed not to understand its meaning
They accepted payment for religious rulings they knew were wrong
questions.explanation: The irrationality is that the Ahbar preached belief in Prophet Muhammad ﷺ — whose coming was described in the Torah they recited — while refusing to believe in him themselves. They taught a position they did not hold, which is a self-contradicting stance.

questions.question: In the tafseer of Ayah 45, what does صَبْر (Sabr) specifically mean?
options: Restraining oneself from responding to the taunts and mockery of disbelievers
Patience specifically in the face of physical hardship, illness, or death
Bearing the burden of Shari'ah obligations (تَكَالِيف شَرْعِيَّة) — enduring what the self finds difficult in fulfilling religious duties
Enduring the loss of worldly wealth and status for the sake of faith
questions.explanation: In this context, Sabr is not general patience in hardship. It specifically means bearing the burden of Shari'ah obligations (takalif shar'iyyah) — enduring what the self finds difficult when fulfilling religious duties.

questions.question: How do scholars interpret يَظُنُّونَ in Ayah 46 when it describes the belief of الْخَاشِعِين (Khashi'in)?
options: As speculation based on the signs of the Day of Judgment but not yet confirmed
As general awareness without the depth of conviction characteristic of the Prophets
As firm, decisive belief (اعْتِقَادًا جَازِمًا) without any trace of doubt, elevated to certainty by context
As hopeful expectation — they sincerely hope to meet Allah but lack complete certainty
questions.explanation: Scholars interpret يَظُنُّونَ here as اعْتِقَادًا جَازِمًا لَا يُخَالِجُهُ شَكّ — firm, decisive belief without any doubt. The context of the Khashi'in's certainty about meeting Allah acts as a qarinah that elevates this usage of dhann to the level of yaqeen.

questions.question: Which of the following was one of the three specific categories through which Allah preferred Bani Israel above the worlds of their time, as described in Ayah 47?
options: He gave them the longest lifespans recorded in any nation
He sent many Prophets and Messengers from among them
He granted them military victory over every enemy they encountered
He made their land the most fertile and inviolable on earth
questions.explanation: The three categories of preference were: (1) Allah sent many Prophets and Messengers from among them; (2) He revealed divine books to them; (3) He made some of them rulers and kings — Dawud and Sulayman ﷺ combined prophethood with kingship.

questions.question: Ayah 48 describes four conditions of the Day of Judgment for the disbelievers. Which of the following is one of those four?
options: No intercession shall be accepted for them
They will witness the punishment but be granted a final opportunity to repent
They will be questioned about every blessing they received in the world
Their good deeds will be weighed but found to be insufficient
questions.explanation: The four conditions are: (1) no soul shall avail another soul anything; (2) no intercession shall be accepted; (3) no ransom or compensation shall be taken from them; (4) no helper can protect them from Allah's punishment.

questions.question: The prescribed tawbah for calf worship in Ayah 54 required an extraordinary act. What was its central requirement?
options: The entire community making pilgrimage to Bayt al-Maqdis as expiation
The innocent (بَرِيء) among Bani Israel killing the guilty (مُجْرِم)
Every member of Bani Israel fasting for forty consecutive days
The guilty publicly confessing their sin before the entire community
questions.explanation: The prescribed tawbah required the innocent (bari') among Bani Israel to kill the guilty (mujrim). This was a specific divine command for that sin. Willingness to submit to this difficult act was itself rida' bi-hukm Allah, and Allah accepted their repentance when they carried it out.

questions.question: The teacher states that وَإِذْ at the beginning of each verse in Ayaat 49–54 implies an understood verb. What is that verb?
options: اشْكُرُوا — Be grateful (for the blessing of...)
اعْتَبِرُوا — Take heed (from the lesson of...)
تَأَمَّلُوا — Reflect deeply (upon the event of...)
أُذْكُرُوا — Remember (My blessing at the time when...)
questions.explanation: The implied understood verb before each وَإِذْ is أُذْكُرُوا — 'Remember.' This structure creates specific enumeration, recounting each blessing individually rather than in general, which is more rhetorically powerful and more conducive to gratitude.

questions.question: تَقْرِيع (Taqri'a), the tone Allah uses toward the Ahbar in Ayah 44, derives from which verbal root and Bab?
options: قَرَنَ يَقْرِنُ — Bab Mufaa'ala
قَرَّبَ يُقَرِّبُ — Bab Tafa'ul
كَرَّعَ يُقَرِّعُ — Bab Taf'eel
قَرَأَ يَقْرَأُ — Bab Ifa'al
questions.explanation: تَقْرِيع means pointed formal rebuke. It derives from the root كَرَّعَ يُقَرِّعُ in Bab Taf'eel, and describes the accusatory and reproving tone of Ayah 44 directed at the Ahbar (Jewish scholars).

questions.question: According to the tafseer, why is Salah described as easy specifically for الْخَاشِعِين (Khashi'in) and not for others?
options: They are experienced worshippers for whom habit has removed the physical difficulty
They are excused from the longer required portions of the prayer
They have memorized more Quran, so recitation during salah requires little effort
Their hearts are already oriented toward Allah, making outward worship a natural expression of their inner state
questions.explanation: The Khashi'in are those whose inner souls are pure and devoted solely to Allah. Salah is easy for them because their hearts are already oriented toward Allah, so the outward act is a natural expression of what is already present within.

questions.question: What does الْفُرْقَان (Furqan) mean as a descriptive name for the Tawrat in Ayah 53?
options: The law that abrogates and supersedes all previously revealed rulings
The book that was revealed across multiple languages and dialects
The criterion that distinguishes حَقّ (truth) from بَاطِل (falsehood)
The scripture memorized in its entirety by the community entrusted with it
questions.explanation: Furqan means 'the criterion' — that which distinguishes haqq (truth) from batil (falsehood). It is a functional title for the Tawrat (and similarly the Quran) based on the book's purpose of differentiating right from wrong.

questions.question: In Ayah 49, what was the stated divine purpose of subjecting Bani Israel to the بَلَاء (Bala') of Fir'aun's oppression?
options: To distinguish the righteous (صَالِح) from the wicked (فَاجِر)
To demonstrate Allah's power and dominion over the greatest empire of the time
To prepare them spiritually for receiving the Torah on Mount Sinai
To punish them for sins committed by their ancestors
questions.explanation: بَلَاء means divine trial or test. The stated divine purpose was to distinguish the righteous (salih) from the wicked (talih/fajir) — the severe test was a means of differentiation, not mere punishment.

questions.question: Beyond simply the act of creating, what does the Divine Name بَارِئ (Bari') convey about its root بَرَأَ?
options: One who creates from nothing without any prior material
One who creates while being completely free from all fault and deficiency
One who creates with full knowledge of every future consequence
One who creates and then sustains creation without any cessation
questions.explanation: بَارِئ comes from بَرَأَ يَبْرَأُ, which carries the meaning of being free from fault and deficiency. So this Divine Name means not only 'the Creator' but one who creates while being completely free from all imperfection — one of the Asma' al-Husna.

questions.question: Why is it significant that Ayah 46 uses ظَنّ — not يَقِين — yet scholars describe the belief of the Khashi'in as اعْتِقَادًا جَازِمًا (firm, decisive belief)?
options: The context (قَرِينَة) of the Khashi'in's certainty about the Day of Judgment elevates this ظَنّ to the level of يَقِين
The scholars view ظَنّ as actually stronger than يَقِين in this specific theological context
ظَنّ and يَقِين are grammatically interchangeable in Quranic Arabic and carry identical weight
Using ظَنّ shows that even the most certain believers retain a small degree of doubt as a form of humility
questions.explanation: This is a contextually elevated usage of ظَنّ. The Khashi'in's certainty about meeting Allah functions as a qarinah (contextual indicator) that elevates the ظَنّ here to the level of يَقِين — it is اعْتِقَادًا جَازِمًا لَا يُخَالِجُهُ شَكّ (decisive belief without any doubt).

questions.question: In Ayah 49, آلُ فِرْعَوْن (Al Fir'aun) specifically includes which range of people?
options: Only those who personally and directly participated in oppressing Bani Israel
Fir'aun's family, close companions, followers, and army
The Egyptian ruling class, excluding the military forces
Only Fir'aun's biological children and wives
questions.explanation: آل derives from أَهْل. In this ayah, آلُ فِرْعَوْن covers Fir'aun's family, close companions, followers, and army — referring specifically to his tyrannical forces who carried out the oppression of Bani Israel.

questions.question: The Divine Name تَوَّاب (Tawwab) closes Ayah 54. What does its intensive مُبَالَغَة pattern (فَعَّال) indicate about Allah's attribute?
options: He accepts repentance abundantly, repeatedly, and even for grave sins — without limit
He accepts repentance only when offered sincerely before the moment of death
He accepts repentance exclusively from those who have never repeated the same sin
He accepts repentance once per sin, requiring new repentance for each repeated offense
questions.explanation: The فَعَّال pattern is the intensive (mubalaghah) form. For تَوَّاب, it indicates that Allah's acceptance of tawbah is vast, repeated, and without limit — He accepts repentance abundantly, even for grave sins, and this attribute has no ceiling.

questions.question: What is the specifically fiqhi reasoning the Ahnaf give for preferring إِسْفَار (Isfar) as the time for Fajr prayer?
options: It ensures enough time remains to repeat the prayer with تِوَال الْمُفَصَّل (Tiwal al-Mufassal) if it becomes Fasid
It ensures the congregation reaches its largest size when people are fully awake
It is safer because Fajr Sadiq is difficult to determine precisely in cloudy conditions
It matches the documented practice of the Prophet ﷺ in the vast majority of his Fajr prayers
questions.explanation: The Hanafi reasoning is practical validity: delaying Fajr until Isfar ensures there is still enough time that if something invalidates the prayer (making it Fasid), the person can repeat it with Tiwal al-Mufassal before Fajr time expires.

questions.question: According to Imam Abu Hanifa, when does the time for Asr begin?
options: When the sun descends to a 45-degree angle in the afternoon sky
When the shadow reaches once (1×) the original length of the object
When the shadow reaches one-and-a-half (1.5×) times the original length
When the shadow of every object reaches twice (2×) its original length beyond the base shadow at zawal
questions.explanation: Imam Abu Hanifa holds that Asr begins when the shadow reaches twice (2×) the original length. The majority — including Imam Muhammad, Imam Abu Yusuf, and the three other major Imams — hold that it begins at once (1×) the original length.

questions.question: What dalil do the Ahnaf rely on for their position that تَرْجِيع (Tarjih) is not part of the Adhan?
options: The general Hanafi principle that Adhan phrases must not be doubled or repeated
The Hadith of Abu Mahzura in Tirmizi, which describes a different sequence
The lifelong practice of Bilal (RA), who never used Tarjih throughout his years of calling the Adhan
A hadith specifically requiring the voice to remain at a consistent volume throughout
questions.explanation: The Ahnaf rely on the lifelong practice of Bilal (RA), who was the Prophet's ﷺ primary Muazzin and never used Tarjih. His consistent practice establishes the standard Hanafi form of the Adhan.

questions.question: Why is the ruling stricter for calling the إِقَامَة (Iqamah) without Wudu than for calling the Adhan without Wudu?
options: The Iqamah is fard while the Adhan is only sunnah, demanding a higher standard of purity
The congregation is physically present and witnesses the Iqamah, making purity more visibly required
Leaving to make Wudu after the Iqamah creates a gap between the Iqamah and the start of salah, disrupting the congregation
The Iqamah is always performed inside the mosque where a higher standard of purity applies
questions.explanation: The Iqamah is the immediate signal for the congregation to begin salah. If the Mu'azzin calls Iqamah without Wudu and then leaves to purify himself, it creates a disruptive gap between the Iqamah and the start of salah — which is the reason the ruling is stricter.

questions.question: If combining prayers is genuinely impossible during a flight, what is the dominant Hanafi Muftabih ruling?
options: Pray one salah during its time in the air and immediately repeat the other upon landing
Let the salah become Qada and make up both prayers as Qasr upon reaching the destination
Pray both salahs consecutively in the air regardless of which time has entered
Temporarily adopt the Shafi'i ruling permitting combination for that specific journey
questions.explanation: The Hanafi Muftabih position does not permit pulling prayers forward to combine them. If genuine combination is impossible, the dominant ruling is to let the salah become Qada and make up both as Qasr at the destination. Temporarily adopting another madhab's ruling for convenience is not valid.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the two applications of the Hanafi حُكْم الرُّبْع (One-Fourth Rule) within the Shurut al-Salah?
options: Najasa covering ¼ or more of the clothing renders the salah invalid
One-fourth of a fard element can be compensated by an additional nafl act
If the Qibla direction is within ¼ of a full turn the salah remains valid
Salah is valid if at least ¼ of the prescribed time has elapsed before starting
questions.explanation: The One-Fourth Rule states 'the quarter is like the whole' (الرُّبْع كَالْكُلّ). Two applications in Shurut al-Salah: (1) Najasa on clothing — less than ¼ is overlooked, ¼ or more invalidates; (2) 'Awra exposure — less than ¼ of an 'awra part does not invalidate, ¼ or more does.

questions.question: A person discovers mid-prayer that they were facing the wrong Qibla direction. What must they do?
options: Turn toward the correct Qibla only at the start of the next Ruku'
Stop the prayer immediately and restart it from the beginning facing the correct direction
Perform اسْتِدَارَة (Istidarah) — turn immediately toward the correct Qibla and continue the prayer
Complete the current prayer as-is and then repeat it fully facing the correct Qibla
questions.explanation: Upon discovering the error mid-prayer, the person must perform Istidarah — immediately turning toward the correct Qibla and continuing the prayer from that point. This differs from discovering the error after the prayer, where the ruling depends on whether Tahharri was performed beforehand.

questions.question: Does إِسْفَار (Isfar) refer to praying in full darkness, at the moment true dawn appears, or when daylight has visibly spread?
options: At mid-morning once the sun has risen well above the horizon
When it is still in full darkness before true dawn (Fajr Sadiq)
At the exact moment true dawn (Fajr Sadiq) first appears on the horizon
When daylight has visibly spread across the sky
questions.explanation: Isfar is when daylight has visibly spread across the sky — not full darkness and not merely the first appearance of true dawn. This is the Hanafi preferred time for Fajr, based on the fiqhi reasoning of ensuring time for repetition if the prayer becomes Fasid.

questions.question: تَرَسُّل (Tarassul) — measured pausing between words — is Masnoon in which call to prayer?
options: The Adhan only
The Iqamah only
Both the Adhan and the Iqamah equally
Neither — both the Adhan and Iqamah use Hadar (rapid continuous speech)
questions.explanation: Tarassul (measured pausing) is Masnoon specifically in the Adhan. The Iqamah uses Hadar — quick, continuous speech — which is the opposite of Tarassul. Using Tarassul in the Iqamah would be incorrect.

questions.question: In تَثْوِيب (Tasweeb) for the Fajr Adhan, after which phrase is الصَّلَاةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ النَّوْمِ inserted?
options: After اللهُ أَكْبَرُ (Allahu Akbar) at the very end of the Adhan
After أَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللهِ (the second Shahadah)
After حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاح (Hayya 'alal-falah)
After حَيَّ عَلَى الصَّلَاة (Hayya 'alas-salah)
questions.explanation: الصَّلَاةُ خَيْرٌ مِنَ النَّوْمِ (Prayer is better than sleep) is inserted after حَيَّ عَلَى الْفَلَاح (Hayya 'alal-falah) in the Fajr Adhan only. This addition is known as Tasweeb and is specific to the dawn call to prayer.

questions.question: تَقْرَار (Taqrar) — repeating the phrases of the Iqamah twice — is derived from the practice of which Muazzin?
options: Bilal (RA)
Sa'd al-Qaraz (RA)
Abu Mahzura (RA)
Ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
questions.explanation: Taqrar is derived from the practice of Abu Mahzura (RA). Bilal (RA) did not use Taqrar in his Iqamah, which is why Imam Shafi'i and Imam Ahmad followed the non-Taqrar form. The Hanafi inclusion of Taqrar comes from the Abu Mahzura tradition.

questions.question: Does the One-Fourth Rule (حُكْم الرُّبْع) apply to نَجَاسَة مُخَفَّفَة (Najasa Mukhaffafa) for the purpose of salah validity?
options: Yes — but only when the Najasa Mukhaffafa is visibly apparent to the naked eye
No — a different half-rule (حُكْم النِّصْف) applies to Najasa Mukhaffafa instead
No — Najasa Mukhaffafa is always overlooked regardless of the amount present
Yes — the same One-Fourth Rule applies as for Najasa Ghaleeza
questions.explanation: The One-Fourth Rule applies to Najasa Mukhaffafa (e.g., urine of animals whose meat is permissible) in the same way as to Najasa Ghaleeza for salah validity — less than ¼ is overlooked, ¼ or more invalidates — though Mukhaffafa is a lighter legal category overall.

questions.question: For a free woman (حُرَّة) in salah, which parts of the body are NOT 'awra according to the Ahnaf?
options: The face, hands, and feet up to the ankles
The hands and arms up to the elbows
The face and the hands up to the wrists
The face only — all other parts must be covered
questions.explanation: According to the Ahnaf, for a free woman (hurra) in salah, only the face and the hands up to the wrists are not 'awra. The entire rest of the body must be covered, and some fuqaha' also include the feet as 'awra in salah.

questions.question: If a person performs تَحَرِّي (Tahharri) before salah and later discovers they faced the wrong Qibla, what is the ruling on their salah?
options: The salah must be repeated because the Qibla condition was objectively not fulfilled
The salah must be repeated if they faced exactly opposite the Qibla — as Imam Shafi'i requires
The salah is valid and does not need to be repeated
The salah is valid only if they were within 45 degrees of the correct direction
questions.explanation: If Tahharri (diligent effort to determine the correct Qibla) was performed before the salah, the prayer is valid and does not need to be repeated even if the person was wrong. If no Tahharri was made at all, repetition is required. The Ahnaf do not add the additional condition that Imam Shafi'i requires for facing exactly opposite.

questions.question: In Hanafi fiqh, what is the ruling if Takbir al-Tahrimah is made before the نِيَّة (Niyyah) is formed?
options: The salah is Makruh but valid and does not need to be repeated
The salah requires a prostration of forgetfulness (سُجُود السَّهْو) to compensate
The salah is valid as long as the intention is formed before the first Ruku'
The salah is invalid per Zahir al-Riwayah
questions.explanation: Per Zahir al-Riwayah (the authoritative Hanafi transmission), the salah is invalid if Takbir al-Tahrimah is made before the Niyyah is formed. Verbalization of the intention is recommended (sunnah) but not obligatory; however, the intention itself must precede or coincide with the opening Takbir.
